papers.title: eFEL: Electrophysiology Feature Extraction Library
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Electrophysiological recordings are essential in experimental and computational neuroscience, providing insights into neuronal excitability and network behaviour. Extracting features such as action potential thresholds, widths, and firing patterns is conceptually straightforward, but in practice it is complicated by heterogeneous datasets and software environments, which hinder reproducibility and interoperability. A standardised, efficient, and portable framework is needed to ensure consistent analysis across platforms and alignment with community data standards. Results We present the Electrophysiology Feature Extraction Library (eFEL) , a cross-platform, open-source library that implements standardised definitions for over 90 electrophysiological features. eFEL combines a high-performance C ++ core with a Python interface, supporting customisable feature dependencies, caching, and parallelisation. It integrates with community standards such as NWB and works seamlessly with common electrophysiology formats and simulation environments. Since its initial release in 2015, eFEL has been used in published studies spanning single-cell analysis, model optimisation, multimodal fitting, and circuit simulations. eFEL provides a FAIR-compliant, versatile resource for reproducible electrophysiological data analysis. Availability and implementation The eFEL library is publicly available at https://github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL and the associated study data and scripts have been deposited in Zenodo at https://zenodo.org/records/17241835

电生理记录在实验神经科学与计算神经科学中至关重要，它们能够帮助我们深入了解神经元的兴奋性及神经网络的行为特征。提取动作电位阈值、波形宽度及放电模式等特征在理论上是相对简单的，但实际上由于数据集的异质性以及不同软件环境的影响，这一过程变得十分复杂，这些因素严重阻碍了研究的可重复性与互操作性。因此，亟需一个标准化、高效且易于使用的框架，以确保跨平台分析的一致性，并使研究结果符合行业数据标准。

papers.title: GLiNER-BioMed: A Suite of Efficient Models for Open Biomedical Named Entity Recognition
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Biomedical named entity recognition (NER) presents unique challenges due to specialized vocabularies, the sheer volume of entities, and the continuous emergence of novel entities. Traditional NER models, constrained by fixed taxonomies and human annotations, struggle to generalize beyond predefined entity types. Results To address these issues, we introduce GLiNER-BioMed, a domain-adapted suite of GLiNER models for biomedicine. Our approach first distills the annotation capabilities of large language models (LLMs) into a smaller, more efficient model, enabling the generation of high-coverage biomedical NER data. We subsequently train two GLiNER architectures, uni- and bi-encoder, at multiple scales to balance computational efficiency and performance. Experiments on eight biomedical datasets demonstrate that GLiNER-BioMed achieved state-of-the-art zero-shot performance (micro-F1 59.77%), exceeding the strongest baseline by 5.96 points (p < 0.001). In few-shot learning, the bi-encoder variant reached 70.39% (10-shot), consistently outperforming the strongest baseline across all settings (p < 0.05). Our findings show that the uni-encoder GLiNER-BioMed achieves the strongest zero-shot performance, while the bi-encoder offers superior few-shot gains and substantially higher inference throughput (+39–568%), making it well-suited to annotation-limited, latency-sensitive, or large-label-space settings. Ablation studies further indicate that combining synthetic biomedical pre-training with general-domain post-training is essential for capturing domain-specific knowledge while maintaining precision-recall balance. Availability and implementation The source code, datasets, and models are publicly available at https://github.com/ds4dh/GLiNER-biomed

生物医学领域中的命名实体识别面临诸多挑战：这些领域存在专门的术语体系，实体数量庞大，且新的实体类型不断涌现。传统的命名实体识别模型受限于固定的分类体系和人工标注数据，难以泛化到未预定义的实体类型上。为解决这些问题，我们开发了GLiNER-BioMed——这套专为生物医学领域设计的GLiNER模型系列。我们的方法首先将大型语言模型的标注能力提取并整合到一个更小、更高效的模型中，从而生成覆盖范围广泛的生物医学命名实体识别数据；随后，我们在不同规模上训练了单编码器与双编码器两种架构，以平衡计算效率与性能。在八个生物医学数据集上的实验表明，GLiNER-BioMed在零样本学习任务中取得了顶尖的性能（微F1分数高达59.77%），其表现比最强的基线模型高出5.96个百分点（p < 0.001）；在少样本学习场景下，双编码器版本的表现更为优异，10次训练后的准确率达到了70.39%，在所有测试设置中均显著优于最强基线模型（p < 0.05）。我们的研究结果表明：单编码器版本的GLiNER-BioMed在零样本学习任务中表现最佳，而双编码器版本则在少样本学习场景下具有更显著的性能提升，并且其推理效率也明显更高（提升了39%至568%），因此它特别适合那些标注数据有限、对响应速度要求较高或实体数量庞大的应用场景。进一步的研究还表明，将合成生物医学数据用于预训练，再结合通用领域的后训练数据，对于帮助模型掌握领域特定知识并保持精确度与召回率的平衡至关重要。

Results To address these issues, we introduce GLiNER-BioMed, a domain-adapted suite of GLiNER models for biomedicine. Our approach first distills the annotation capabilities of large language models (LLMs) into a smaller, more efficient model, enabling the generation of high-coverage biomedical NER data. We subsequently train two GLiNER architectures, uni- and bi-encoder, at multiple scales to balance computational efficiency and performance. Experiments on eight biomedical datasets demonstrate that GLiNER-BioMed achieved state-of-the-art zero-shot performance (micro-F1 59.77%), exceeding the strongest baseline by 5.96 points (p < 0.001). In few-shot learning, the bi-encoder variant reached 70.39% (10-shot), consistently outperforming the strongest baseline across all settings (p < 0.05). papers.title: CryoPromptSeg: Prompt-guided Segmentation with Integrated Denoising for Cryo-EM Particle Picking
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Cryo-electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) single particle analysis (SPA) is a key technique for revealing the structure of biomacromolecules by three-dimensional reconstruction. Achieving high-resolution reconstruction relies on the acquisition of a large number of authentic particles; however, manual particle picking is inefficient and inadequate for the demands of reconstruction, making automated particle picking a major research focus. Although the foundational segmentation model Segment Anything Model (SAM) has recently advanced automated particle picking, its segmentation advantages have not been fully realized in cryo-EM applications. Moreover, cryo-EM images often have significant noise. Conventional denoising decreases noise but frequently overlooks high-level semantic information, leading to oversmoothed particle regions and reduced particle distinguishability. Results To address these challenges, we propose CryoPromptSeg, which employs prompt-guided SAM for particle picking while integrating a semantically enhanced image denoiser. Specifically, by performing domain adaptation fine-tuning of SAM and incorporating prompts generated by the proposed automatic prompt generator, it achieves precise segmentation of cryo-EM particles. In addition, it employs a parallel multi-task framework to jointly train the denoiser and the prompt generator, incorporating particle semantic information from the prompt generator into the denoiser to suppress noise while preserving highly distinguishable particle structures. To lower the barrier to practical application, we developed a user-friendly online prediction platform for particle picking. Experimental results demonstrate that CryoPromptSeg outperforms existing mainstream methods in both particle picking accuracy and image denoising quality, thus providing a novel solution for the automation of particle picking. Availability The code and platform are available at: https://github.com/347251369/CryoPromptSeg

papers.title: 3D Registration-Guided Deformable Residual Inpainting for ssEM Restoration
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Serial section Electron Microscopy (ssEM) is essential for studying biological cell structures at nanometer resolution. However, Supporting Film Folding (SFF) degradation frequently occurs during sample preparation, causing structural distortions and information loss that severely impair downstream analyses such as 3D reconstruction and neuron segmentation. Results We propose RegInpaint, a novel recovery framework that jointly addresses deformation correction and missing-information restoration caused by SFF degradation. RegInpaint formulates SFF recovery as a joint problem of 3D elastic registration and image inpainting, providing a generalizable solution for ssEM restoration. Experiments on four EM datasets show that RegInpaint consistently outperforms existing methods in image restoration quality and significantly improves neuron segmentation accuracy. Availability Source code is freely available at https://github.com/zhangzhenbang2021/RegInpaint.git

all_papers.title: eFEL: Electrophysiology Feature Extraction Library
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Electrophysiological recordings are essential in experimental and computational neuroscience, providing insights into neuronal excitability and network behaviour. Extracting features such as action potential thresholds, widths, and firing patterns is conceptually straightforward, but in practice it is complicated by heterogeneous datasets and software environments, which hinder reproducibility and interoperability. A standardised, efficient, and portable framework is needed to ensure consistent analysis across platforms and alignment with community data standards. Results We present the Electrophysiology Feature Extraction Library (eFEL) , a cross-platform, open-source library that implements standardised definitions for over 90 electrophysiological features. eFEL combines a high-performance C ++ core with a Python interface, supporting customisable feature dependencies, caching, and parallelisation. It integrates with community standards such as NWB and works seamlessly with common electrophysiology formats and simulation environments. Since its initial release in 2015, eFEL has been used in published studies spanning single-cell analysis, model optimisation, multimodal fitting, and circuit simulations. eFEL provides a FAIR-compliant, versatile resource for reproducible electrophysiological data analysis. Availability and implementation The eFEL library is publicly available at https://github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL and the associated study data and scripts have been deposited in Zenodo at https://zenodo.org/records/17241835

all_papers.title: GLiNER-BioMed: A Suite of Efficient Models for Open Biomedical Named Entity Recognition
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Biomedical named entity recognition (NER) presents unique challenges due to specialized vocabularies, the sheer volume of entities, and the continuous emergence of novel entities. Traditional NER models, constrained by fixed taxonomies and human annotations, struggle to generalize beyond predefined entity types. Results To address these issues, we introduce GLiNER-BioMed, a domain-adapted suite of GLiNER models for biomedicine. Our approach first distills the annotation capabilities of large language models (LLMs) into a smaller, more efficient model, enabling the generation of high-coverage biomedical NER data. We subsequently train two GLiNER architectures, uni- and bi-encoder, at multiple scales to balance computational efficiency and performance. Experiments on eight biomedical datasets demonstrate that GLiNER-BioMed achieved state-of-the-art zero-shot performance (micro-F1 59.77%), exceeding the strongest baseline by 5.96 points (p < 0.001). In few-shot learning, the bi-encoder variant reached 70.39% (10-shot), consistently outperforming the strongest baseline across all settings (p < 0.05). Our findings show that the uni-encoder GLiNER-BioMed achieves the strongest zero-shot performance, while the bi-encoder offers superior few-shot gains and substantially higher inference throughput (+39–568%), making it well-suited to annotation-limited, latency-sensitive, or large-label-space settings. Ablation studies further indicate that combining synthetic biomedical pre-training with general-domain post-training is essential for capturing domain-specific knowledge while maintaining precision-recall balance. Availability and implementation The source code, datasets, and models are publicly available at https://github.com/ds4dh/GLiNER-biomed

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
生物医学领域中的命名实体识别面临诸多挑战：这些领域存在专门的术语体系，实体数量庞大，且新的实体类型不断涌现。传统的命名实体识别模型受限于固定的分类体系和人工标注数据，难以泛化到未预定义的实体类型上。为解决这些问题，我们开发了GLiNER-BioMed——这套专为生物医学领域设计的GLiNER模型系列。我们的方法首先将大型语言模型的标注能力提取并整合到一个更小、更高效的模型中，从而生成覆盖范围广泛的生物医学命名实体识别数据；随后，我们在不同规模上训练了单编码器与双编码器两种架构，以平衡计算效率与性能。在八个生物医学数据集上的实验表明，GLiNER-BioMed在零样本学习任务中取得了顶尖的性能（微F1分数高达59.77%），其表现比最强的基线模型高出5.96个百分点（p < 0.001）；在少样本学习场景下，双编码器版本的表现更为优异，10次训练后的准确率达到了70.39%，在所有测试设置中均显著优于最强基线模型（p < 0.05）。我们的研究结果表明：单编码器版本的GLiNER-BioMed在零样本学习任务中表现最佳，而双编码器版本则在少样本学习场景下具有更显著的性能提升，并且其推理效率也明显更高（提升了39%至568%），因此它特别适合那些标注数据有限、对响应速度要求较高或实体数量庞大的应用场景。进一步的研究还表明，将合成生物医学数据用于预训练，再结合通用领域的后训练数据，对于帮助模型掌握领域特定知识并保持精确度与召回率的平衡至关重要。  

**开源与实现方式**  
源代码、数据集及模型均已公开发布，访问地址为：https://github.com/ds4dh/GLiNER-biomed

生物医学领域中的命名实体识别面临诸多挑战：这些领域存在专门的术语体系，实体数量庞大，且新的实体类型不断涌现。传统的命名实体识别模型受限于固定的分类体系和人工标注数据，难以泛化到未预定义的实体类型上。为解决这些问题，我们开发了GLiNER-BioMed——这套专为生物医学领域设计的GLiNER模型系列。我们的方法首先将大型语言模型的标注能力提取并整合到一个更小、更高效的模型中，从而生成覆盖范围广泛的生物医学命名实体识别数据；随后，我们在不同规模上训练了单编码器与双编码器两种架构，以平衡计算效率与性能。在八个生物医学数据集上的实验表明，GLiNER-BioMed在零样本学习任务中取得了顶尖的性能（微F1分数高达59.77%），其表现比最强的基线模型高出5.96个百分点（p < 0.001）；在少样本学习场景下，双编码器版本的表现更为优异，10次训练后的准确率达到了70.39%，在所有测试设置中均显著优于最强基线模型（p < 0.05）。我们的研究结果表明：单编码器版本的GLiNER-BioMed在零样本学习任务中表现最佳，而双编码器版本则在少样本学习场景下具有更显著的性能提升，并且其推理效率也明显更高（提升了39%至568%），因此它特别适合那些标注数据有限、对响应速度要求较高或实体数量庞大的应用场景。进一步的研究还表明，将合成生物医学数据用于预训练，再结合通用领域的后训练数据，对于帮助模型掌握领域特定知识并保持精确度与召回率的平衡至关重要。  

**开源与实现方式**  
源代码、数据集及模型均已公开发布，访问地址为：https://github.com/ds4dh/GLiNER-biomed

all_papers.title: CryoPromptSeg: Prompt-guided Segmentation with Integrated Denoising for Cryo-EM Particle Picking
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Cryo-electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) single particle analysis (SPA) is a key technique for revealing the structure of biomacromolecules by three-dimensional reconstruction. Achieving high-resolution reconstruction relies on the acquisition of a large number of authentic particles; however, manual particle picking is inefficient and inadequate for the demands of reconstruction, making automated particle picking a major research focus. Although the foundational segmentation model Segment Anything Model (SAM) has recently advanced automated particle picking, its segmentation advantages have not been fully realized in cryo-EM applications. Moreover, cryo-EM images often have significant noise. Conventional denoising decreases noise but frequently overlooks high-level semantic information, leading to oversmoothed particle regions and reduced particle distinguishability. Results To address these challenges, we propose CryoPromptSeg, which employs prompt-guided SAM for particle picking while integrating a semantically enhanced image denoiser. Specifically, by performing domain adaptation fine-tuning of SAM and incorporating prompts generated by the proposed automatic prompt generator, it achieves precise segmentation of cryo-EM particles. In addition, it employs a parallel multi-task framework to jointly train the denoiser and the prompt generator, incorporating particle semantic information from the prompt generator into the denoiser to suppress noise while preserving highly distinguishable particle structures. To lower the barrier to practical application, we developed a user-friendly online prediction platform for particle picking. Experimental results demonstrate that CryoPromptSeg outperforms existing mainstream methods in both particle picking accuracy and image denoising quality, thus providing a novel solution for the automation of particle picking. Availability The code and platform are available at: https://github.com/347251369/CryoPromptSeg

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
冷冻电子显微镜单颗粒分析技术是揭示生物大分子三维结构的关键方法。要实现高分辨率重建，必须获取大量真实的颗粒图像；然而，人工挑选颗粒效率低下，无法满足重建需求，因此自动化颗粒挑选成为当前研究的热点。尽管基础的分割模型——Segment Anything Model（SAM）显著提升了自动化颗粒挑选的能力，但其分割优势在冷冻电子显微镜应用中尚未得到充分体现。此外，冷冻电镜图像通常含有大量噪声，传统去噪方法虽然能降低噪声水平，但往往会丢失高层次的语义信息，导致颗粒区域过度平滑、区分度降低。  

为应对这些挑战，我们提出了CryoPromptSeg算法。该算法结合了基于提示的SAM分割技术与语义增强的图像去噪技术：通过针对冷冻电镜数据对SAM模型进行领域适配训练，并利用自主研发的自动提示生成器生成有效的分割提示，从而实现颗粒的高精度识别；同时，采用并行多任务框架协同训练去噪器和提示生成器，使去噪过程能够充分利用颗粒的语义信息，有效抑制噪声的同时保留颗粒结构的清晰度。为降低实际应用门槛，我们还开发了用户友好的在线颗粒挑选预测平台。实验结果表明，CryoPromptSeg在颗粒挑选准确性与图像去噪质量方面均优于现有主流方法，为自动化颗粒挑选技术提供了新的解决方案。  

**代码与平台获取方式**  
相关代码及在线平台可访问：https://github.com/347251369/CryoPromptSeg

all_papers.title: 3D Registration-Guided Deformable Residual Inpainting for ssEM Restoration
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Serial section Electron Microscopy (ssEM) is essential for studying biological cell structures at nanometer resolution. However, Supporting Film Folding (SFF) degradation frequently occurs during sample preparation, causing structural distortions and information loss that severely impair downstream analyses such as 3D reconstruction and neuron segmentation. Results We propose RegInpaint, a novel recovery framework that jointly addresses deformation correction and missing-information restoration caused by SFF degradation. RegInpaint formulates SFF recovery as a joint problem of 3D elastic registration and image inpainting, providing a generalizable solution for ssEM restoration. Experiments on four EM datasets show that RegInpaint consistently outperforms existing methods in image restoration quality and significantly improves neuron segmentation accuracy. all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Serial section Electron Microscopy (ssEM) is essential for studying biological cell structures at nanometer resolution. However, Supporting Film Folding (SFF) degradation frequently occurs during sample preparation, causing structural distortions and information loss that severely impair downstream analyses such as 3D reconstruction and neuron segmentation. Results We propose RegInpaint, a novel recovery framework that jointly addresses deformation correction and missing-information restoration caused by SFF degradation. RegInpaint formulates SFF recovery as a joint problem of 3D elastic registration and image inpainting, providing a generalizable solution for ssEM restoration. Experiments on four EM datasets show that RegInpaint consistently outperforms existing methods in image restoration quality and significantly improves neuron segmentation accuracy.
